title: Iterators and Adapters
summary: The Iterator trait and next, iter, iter_mut and into_iter, laziness, the common adapters (map, filter, filter_map, enumerate, zip, chain, take, skip, rev, flat_map, peekable, windows), consumers (collect, sum, count, fold, any, all, find, position, min_by_key, max_by), collecting into different types including Result, and why iterator chains are as fast as loops.

cards.q: Why does `(1..).map(|n| n * n).filter(|n| n % 3 == 1)` not run forever?
cards.a:
Adapters are lazy: nothing is computed until a consumer asks for values

Building the chain does no work. Only a consumer such as `take(5).collect()` pulls values through, and it stops asking after five.

cards.q: What does collecting an iterator of `Result<T, E>` into `Result<Vec<T>, E>` do?
cards.a:
Gives `Ok` with all the values, or the first `Err`, stopping there

The errors are not skipped: one `Err` makes the whole result that `Err`, and collecting stops at it.
